svg.title: Environment-variable guidance, version 1.1.0
svg.desc: Sanitized application guidance listing missing Jira and Azure DevOps tokens, setup steps, and the Windows environment editor prompt.

g.text: PS C:\ADO-to-Jira> Environment-variable guidance - Version 1.1.0
Missing environment variables:
- JIRA_API_TOKEN (Jira API token)
- AZDO_DEMO_PAT (DEMO Azure DevOps PAT)
- AZDO_TEST_PAT (TEST Azure DevOps PAT)
Create the required tokens if you do not already have them:
Jira API token:
1. Open https://id.atlassian.com/manage-profile/security/api-tokens
2. Select Create API token, enter a label, and create the token.
3. Copy it immediately; Atlassian will not show it again.
4. Store it as JIRA_API_TOKEN in Windows environment variables.
Azure DevOps PAT, once for each organization:
1. Sign in to the Azure DevOps organization.
2. Select your profile icon, then User settings > Personal access tokens.
3. Select New Token, then enter a name and expiration date.
4. Choose the organization and minimum Work Items read access needed.
5. Create the PAT and copy it immediately; it will not be shown again.
6. Store it as AZDO_<PREFIX>_PAT, using each configured prefix.
Add the missing values in Windows:
1. Press the Windows key and search for environment variables.
2. Open Edit the system environment variables.
3. Select Environment Variables.
4. Under User variables, select New.
5. Enter each missing variable name exactly as listed.
6. Enter the matching Jira token or Azure DevOps PAT value.
7. Select OK on each window to save the changes.
8. Close and reopen PowerShell, Command Prompt, or VS Code.
Never put token values in config.json or Git.
Open Windows Environment Variables now to add them? (y/n): y
Opened the Windows Environment Variables window.
After you add the missing values, press Enter to continue...

svg.text: SANITIZED EXAMPLE | TOKEN VALUES ARE NEVER SHOWN
